Folks —

Attached are the artifacts for Marta (see attachments referenced below). Summary of key points included for the CAIQ mapping:

- Rotation model: We use a dual-layer model — a customer DEK (data encryption key) is encrypted under a tenant-specific KEK (key-encryption-key) stored in a managed-cloud KMS. For customer-managed HSMs (BYOK), the KEK wrapping key resides in the HSM and we import an asymmetric wrapping key into the KMS for envelope wrapping.

- Rotation cadence & evidence: Automatic rotation jobs run nightly for eligible keys; manual rotation is available for emergency rotation via the ops console and requires a 2-person approval flow (IAM + Security). The attached rotation-log-20270411.csv contains three rotation events for sample-tenant-123 (redacted tenant name), with columns: key_id,event_type,timestamp,actor,old_key_id,new_key_id,signature_hash.

- Retirement/enforcement: When a key is rotated, a background decryption job rewraps DEKs for snapshots older than the rotation time. Replaced KEKs are set to disable after 7 days and then scheduled for destruction after 30 days; KMS enforces disable/delete lifecycle via key policy and automated workflow (we include the excerpt in kms-access-matrix.xlsx).

- HSM boundary: hsm-workflow-diagram.pdf shows the handoff: HSM generates the asymmetric wrapping key (KEK wrap key), only the wrapped KEK leaves the HSM. KMS stores the wrapped KEK and performs unwrapping within a trusted module or via a customer’s HSM when BYOK is used.

Attachments included: rotation-log-20270411.csv (CSV, redacted), hsm-workflow-diagram.pdf (diagram), kms-access-matrix.xlsx (policy excerpts). I also created rotation-snapshot-20270411.json (machine-readable snapshot) — if you prefer JSON instead of CSV, say the word and I’ll send it.

-- Marcus Lin
Senior Applied Cryptography Engineer
Redwood Inference
